Noodly arms grasped around this sword will be unable to strike with strength or precision.

The wielder's arms, which are more wobbly than this blade, will be unable to strike with strength or precision.
Debug No Crits Rapier of Testing
Frail arms combined with the mighty heft of this singled handed throwable weapon will be unable to strike with strength or precision.
Debug No Crits Hatchet of Testing
No real life accurate to reality human person would be able to wield this mighty weapon with strength or precision.

Might as well grab a much smaller hammer if you want to strike with strength or precision.

The mighty heft and girth of this sword rivals only that of the wielder's arms which is why they will be unable to strike with strength or precision.

For catching the fruit of the sea.
The reflective scales shimmer brightly in the light.
Securely locked, the box pulses with strange energy.
A pirate flag taken from the ship Satisfaction on behalf of the Captain Grace O'Malley.
Specialized tools used by Inquisitor Lucia.
Worn by the Anointed who supported the Inquisition.
Barely legible lists of Brightwood's residents, homes, and property.
Candles used by followers of Inquisitor Matthias to mark those whose souls were deemed strong.
The medallion worn by a notoriously sadistic Inquisitor.
A satchel of some earthy-smelling substance carried by the Dryad warriors.
A powerful catalyst for healing magics.
A secondary component that Eclipse Warriors used in forging Dryad armor.
Bloody cloth with imprinted memories of past menders.
A mysterious flower known for its curative properties.
A pure white, powder salve formulated by soothsayers on Aeternum.
Another component that Dryad warriors used in the forging of armor.
Old, rusty, bent nails from a coffin suggesting it was broken open after being buried underground.
Partially decomposed bones coated in dry dirt.
These human bones appear to have been broken and reformed many, many times.
Specific type of Starmetal, a Starmetal that seems to twinkle even in daylight.
Blades once used by those not afraid of stabbing a friend in the back.
A plank some unlucky pirates were once forced to walk.
Bindings to cruelly restrain prisoners, used by a notorious hangman.
A mysterious liquid that instantly coagulates spilled blood.
Scraps of writing from a mad man.
Assorted tools used by the Corrupted for gathering lumber and mining.
Old twine and chain that appears to have been used to restrain one of the Lost.
Military orders from Reida's Burrow targeting the Lumberyard to serve as a bulwark against the Lost.
Makes armor last twice as long.
One use will last for years.
Worked and reworked for maximum strength.
Strong protection for lining a helm.
Reinforcing metal, made to withstand the worst.
Ore infused with the heat of battle.
For weatherproofing all types of surfaces.
Pieces of the original Battle's Embrace.
Their shine may have faded, but they won't fail in battle.
Nice and thick, protected against everyday wear.
A token that can only come from a grave in Brackwater.
A token that can only come from a grave in Walsham.
A token that can only come from Moira the Unburied.
A token that can only come from a grave in Brightrest.
A focusing orb made by the Ancient mages long ago.
A dispatch sent from Eastburn Outpost that never arrived in Brightwood.
A barbed catfish with particularly nice whiskers.
A hooked squid known for its potent ink.
Packets of Food Supplies for the Rustheart Miners in Brightwood.
A crate of weapons recently forged by the Rustheart Blacksmiths.
A detailed drawing of an extremely effective weapon for forging.
A sheaf of leaves that can be brewed into a Tea the Angry Earth Dryads imbibe.
A sugary substance harvested from Young Trees in Lush Hideway.
A handful of stems collected from Bronzeroot Shamans in the Verdant Cavern.
A handful of spores collected from the remains of Ceran.
A fine golden ring, slightly tarnished from a long period in a bear's digestive tract.
A keepsake from Megara's once-happy life which is almost certain to make her sad.
The journal of Megara Pantasazi from the happiest times in her life.
A letter from Megara's Lost Husband, saying he's giving up so he won't bring her down.
A tattered and rumpled cloak, bearing the Soulwarden insignia.
A piece of polished jade. When viewed closely, you can faintly make out the name "Patricia".
A set of rusted keys to a chest in Slumbering Echoes.
A collection of the stones that Dryad Archers integrate into their bodies.
A sack of supplies, stolen by the Corrupted from the Soulwardens.
A vial containing a thick black fluid. Smells awful, and no one should taste it.
A chunk of high quality ore from the Defiler Excavation.
A splinter of Azoth, recovered from a broken Ancient statue.
A blackened talisman of unknown origin, bearing a simple symbol.
A blackened talisman of unknown origin, bearing a simple symbol.

A cruel weapon, often used by barbarians to put a damper on good times.
What are you willing to put on the line?
Despite every link in the chain burning red hot, it keeps it's structural strength.
What is a flail, if not a metal whip?
"You call to it, and it's there, when you need it most."
It's adorned with various unknown sigils.
It ends things quicker than lengthy negotiations.
A ferocious weapon and a magnificent show.
Some are leaders, and some are followers. But even a follower can have greatness.
A weapon that will provide you with more than enough proof of your conquest.
"You have free will, why do you use it for evil?"
Humble in appearance, this weapon is far stronger than you may think.
A weapon that could only be forged by one seeking only brutality.
"Of course I have a plan, I start swingin."
Hellish flames trail its every swing.
An excellent choice to acquire some prisoners of war.
At times this flail seems like an unstoppable force.
Although called Fairfight, using it in a fight is anything but fair.
A reliable weapon for any member of a standard fighting force.
Knock your foes down and don't show them any mercy.
"Whoever named this must be a fool. Flails go around shields, they don't destroy shields."
Strike your foes and rend their flesh away.
A strike upside the head is as good a technique as any in a fight.
A dangerous weapon used by many well-trained and well-equipped warriors.
The keepers of the forest can't always let it grow unchecked.
Many souls have inhabited this flail over the aeons. And when your time comes, you shall be the next.
The depths below have caught you, and they don't intend to let go.
"You named this Omnidestructor? Your naming sense is apparently as bad as your workmanship."
A heavenly weapon, a thoughful gift given to someone centuries ago.
Some noble souls simply seek to protect others, no matter the context.
"Never imagined a flail to be effective at sea, yet an ancient sea captain proved it so."
"Beneath one war there always lies many more."
One swing is enough to paralyze.
You hear its distant calls, calls for murder.
A shriek Raven's call precedes every slaughter this weapon aids in.
"I've never seen a flail used like that before."
Prepared to protect, in even the coldest of places.
A trusty flail, it never seems to break and is ready for any threat.
The battle always shifts when this glorious weapon arrives.
This flail has been passed down for a long time, repaired and reconstructed numerous times.
A weapon that will last you to the very end.
You can just barely make out what its saying.... "Duck!"
"Look after all others as if they are yourself."
Just when you think you've safely dodge the first strike, the second is already here.
Adorned with moon imagery, its believed to be dedicated to an ancient moon goddess.
A solid piece of gear, it's metal is perfect for bashing dangers of a jungle.
Few bodies are left standing once this weapon enter's the battle.
You can't quite tell, but it seems as if theres a human presence somewhere deep in the flail.
Perfect for clearing out street rats.
Provides a very short life sentence.
"It's reappeared often throughout history, always in service of a new King"
Flames spit out from it when swung.
Once it starts swinging, its unstoppable.
Great power used by Great Evil.
"The undertaker smiles, he knows this weapon is good for business."
It's said that the one with this weapon is always mysteriously awoken when a danger is near.
It glistens gracefully in the morning sun.
"A very serious weapon, for very serious people."
You'll need repentance after the sins you commit with this weapon.
It's reach is farther than it appears.
No matter how much havoc it wreaks, it never has a splash of blood on it.
A simple flail, but extraordinarily powerful.
A weapon that sniffs out the weak.
An unseen bond ties you to this weapon.
Sometimes, you just gotta break things.
"Few things are more powerful than spite."
Although appearing as if never used, this weapon has seen countless battles.
A mythic oath powers both this weapon and its wielder.
Some believe it takes more strength to break your oath than to keep it.
Even a light hit from this weapon is potentially lethal.
"It protects us at night, and we protect it during day."
An unmatched weapon that even the most dignified nobility can't help but seeth at.
"At its end you will find its beginning."
"A sweet aroma lingers on the horizon; battle is coming."
Suitable for both saving and slaughtering.
When you've just reached your limit.
Most effective when paired with well laid plans.
Keep threats at a distance, no matter their ferocity.
A light shines from the ball, the sight of it encouraging the wielder's allies, and frightening their foes.
"When you connnect once, just keep hitting."
To a weapon such as this, every life is disposable.
"It's not as low as you may think."
"Keep the ball rolling and the chains swinging."
"It resides deep within, undetectable until ignited by the flames of war."
When wielded properly, it draws glorious arcs of blood across the battlefield.
An incredibly strong weapon, thats incredibly hard to wield.
"For when the real stuff just wont do."
It's never been easier to remove head from body.
Not something you want to be on the receiving end of.
A stain that follows you, from the deepest ocean to the highest tower.
"None truly know it, though some can hear it"
"The force of its hit is matched only by the bodies in the heavens."
"One only truly knows their faith when near death."
"The thorns grew, like a protective measure."

The perfect way to keep warm in the snowy north.
The perfect way to keep warm in the snowy north.
This item has been Deprecated and can be salvaged into other craft mods.
A soft light drew you to find this amulet among all others, like a warm grove in the summer.
"For trees and bushes to have gained sentience on Aeternum, it should be no stretch to even assert they have a soul."
Not exactly primal, but it seems to have such an ancient quality that other words feel almost childlike as a comparison for this small trinket.
This staff draws its power directly from the deep recesses of the earth where the First Lives began.
Winter is an indelible part of the cycle of the years just as death is a reflection of our lives.
The quiet void has never once forgotten the time before beginnings and will never let us stray too far from it either.
"As dangerous as it may be, even fire is an important part of a healthy forest."
Jagged and drought-like to the touch. You wonder if it was meant to harm the victim or the wielder.
You can barely read a simple name is engraved on the hilt, 'Clint'.
An absolute mountain of a woman. Morgol was feared in many corners of Aeternum for her size rather than her temperament.
A simple but elegant name, for a simple but elegant shield.
"It may not be as sturdy as iron, but such old azoth touched wood must be sturdy enough, no?"
If shot true, arrows from this bow seem to dance and scream through the air as they chase a target.
Fertilizer is a necessity to caretake a forest of this size and, well, something has to make all of it.
"As the land shifts through time, so too do travelers shift through the land. Leaving all their bloody trash too!"
A bolt of lightning from the blue opened a tree and this fell out. Don't ask me how it got there, I don't know either.
Long thought to be an old wives tale, perhaps such cryptic creatures ended up in Aeternum.
As wyrdwood grows taller and taller, it must reach further, and further to find azoth in the soil. Not every root finds the nutrients, and must be abandoned by the trees.
A strange tool to any who are not native caretakers of the forest.
It seems to be less of a coat, and moreso a… piece of a cocoon…? But what insect could even be large enough to molt shards this large?
This hat has seen many heads in its travels. I really wouldn't recommend wearing it though.
These pants are soft enough that you feel you can remember what it was like to swing in the treetops.
Such heavy boots are invaluable while crossing swamps and moors. Though the denizens of such lands won't appreciate your intrusions.
Simple but tough leather is invaluable when trying to gather berries from their protective bushels of thorns.
It's better to go with the flow, than to vainly fight against it.
This seems to be a keepsake from some kind of graverobbing scum.
The extremely dense stones in its craftsmanship have allowed mages to infuse a great deal more azoth into this earring than you would expect.
"Just as we must shepherd those through life, we must also ensure they are guided in death."
While this may be an ice gauntlet, you'd be a fool to assume the only rock it throws is blue.
An invaluable tool for a guiding cleric. It may not serve you as well in combat as it did its previous owner at the altar.
"You stole my firewood to make a staff? I guess you can keep it, but, why not just go cut down a tree…?"
The second wind is where champions and warriors are made. Usually because that's when people end up dead, and you can't be a winner if you lost.
Don't let the rough craftsmanship fool you, it's as sharp as it needs to be to stab you.
The weight of Winter is more than most expect.
Shields have served many well over the milennia. You'd be wise to not ignore them.
You can feel the fate of the planet in your hands. Fight well.
A frost coated arrow has quite the shock to it when it pierces flesh.
Its blast signals the start of the fight, and the end of a life.
Formation and organization are almost alien concepts to a battlefield such as Aeternum.
"Aim for the back, not only because it’s a bloody large open space, but because it will disrupt your opponent's rhythm and set them on edge."
A heavy piece of stone that fell off the ceiling of an ancient cave. Or did it come from the ground?
This blade did not come from a boulder, but due to its size, that's a very reasonable assumption.
Even after centuries of weathering and damage, this helm stands as strong as the Pantheon itself.
You feel the slow, muttering prayer of the land while you wear this helmet.
The weight of these leg guards is so great you feel that you can't be moved. Which does pose a problem, as walking tends to be important.
"Gary I hate you so much. Gloves are gloves and shoes are shoes, these aren't even similar."
"Reg, do you think you could wear these on your feet? Gloves are kinda like shoes but for your hands!"
A small seed pod. It seems the wild growth is spreading further and faster than you could have thought.
It seems to have been cleansed and brought into new life. Though what caused such densely corrupted metal to change may be beyond your ken.
The corruption contained within this trinket has been satisfied. For now.
This staff seems to have resisted the opaque corruption surrounding it, perhaps due to the earnest prayers of the monk who used to walk with it.
Another strange magical item for such a densely corrupted deathtrap. Though this one seems to still be in the process of its cleansing. How powerful must this cleansing force be?
The void flows through you to grant you power. As long as you keep it fed, it will keep you strong.
A strange choice of weapon, but staves have been a reliable choice for many people defending themselves over the years.
Powerful thrusts to turn your foes to dust.
Not a very imposing weapon, but certainly one that will be quite dangerous in skilled hands.
A warrior's will of iron cannot simply be shattered.
Such straightforward worksmanship is always something you can rely on. However, it's really quite strange that such a simple shield hasn't yet been corrupted.
Spending so much time in the depths of the void will change even the most immutable of materials.
As you feel the depths drag you down, your eyes turn further upwards.
It seems to be a fallen relic from a failed expedition.
If you're willing to step into a strange space you may find this musket to be a reliable partner.
Just be careful not to get dizzy.
The corruption doesn't seem to have sharpened the blade, though you're certain it's significantly more dangerous.
It was dropped from the heavens, as if to curse the malignant corruption.
An overflowing confidence from the commander as she leads her men on an ill-fated expedition.
A foolish wanderer to have delved into such malignant corruption in the hungering greed for glittering gold.
You feel that this helm has expanded your mind, though you've yet to fill it with anything so it feels rather empty for now.
The unflagging stamina of your demonic foes fills your legs.
The resistance against enduring corruption can never cease.
A poor lost soul left these behind.
An old prayer to protect sailors is imbued within this insignificant trinket.
A certainly stolen token. It's difficult to justify calling it an 'heirloom' if it was taken from a poor soul on the seas.
A fanciful decoration that used to adorn a pirate's ear.
You make do with what you have in a ship on the seas.
Jagged edges and ridged shards fly from its palm. Even the gauntlet itself stabs at you while you wear it.
A burst of strength pours forth from your hand and surges outwards.
A warm light guides you home, and comforts your return.
A dangerous, but invaluable, tool for any scourge of the high seas.
Arguably more ornamental than functional. Though a weapon is a weapon, even on the sea.
Ice usually is not a particularly dangerous rock, but on the sea it becomes for more concerning.
A piece of sodden wood adrift for many years. You feel a sense of kinship to its arrival.
Rogueish individuals may be known for more discreet tools, but really anything will do if their victim's back is turned.
Small jars of oil seem to be enchanted to this bow, though how they are attaching themselves to the arrows it fires remains a syrupy mystery.
You've never known a berserker to be more interested in firing a tool than bludgeoning their foes, but to each their own.
A unique powder blend makes this musket a bit heavier before you fire, though you do certainly feel lighter afterwards.
You aren't sure if this axe was named for a dark cavern or the cold depths of the sea, though its circumstances ceratinly imply the latter.
"Gary, this isn't a cutlass, it's a longsword at best. You can't just call something what it's not. Yes Gary I know we're Pirates but we have bloody standards."
You could argue this to be any old piece of wood, but the sheer size of it implies it must have come from a mast.
The heavy chain makes this flail a bit more unwieldy, but definitely more deadly.
You'll certainly regret wearing something so… mildewy…
A captain always goes down with her ship.
While not particularly protective, these shoes make for excellent comfort while trapped on a slab of wood in the open water.
The gloves make you feel extremely cool.
While they certainly won't keep the cold out, they also aren't keeping the heat in.
The amount of azoth stored in here would astound any scholar.
A burning heat will leave a mark on your finger if you wear this for too long.
Life begets energy and energy begets life.
The comforting warmth of a soft bed protects you.
You can't tell if this gauntlet houses a miserable trapped soul, or is just, really, REALLY cold.
As the void surges forth so too does its hatred at anything within the light.
The flames lick at their victim, as if to consume everything about them, down to the last ash.
A protector is a valiant warrior indeed. For what could be more noble than protecting the weak?
Any tool that can rend metal will most certainly also rend flesh.
"Gary. That's not. Hippopotamidaen isn't a word, Gary. Latin, and also English, don't work that way. And besides, Hippos aren't even real. You shouldn't believe everything a Bard tells you Gary."
A standard military tactic. Shields up, and spears forward.
A weapon more suited to a tavern brawl than a proper duel.
This gun is not so suited for killing foes as much as it suited for wanton destruction.
Not a particularly accurate name, but then again, whomever named it certainly isn't familiar with the proper Pantheon.
Not so much a warrior's weapon as it is an executioner's tool.
Power and energy course through this sword in a way you simply can't comprehend.
The power of the Gods comes down upon your foe.
A weapon out of time, and in a land out of sync.
Those who would steal from dead people and dead lands such as these deserve their grisly fates.
A thick undershirt worn by many Heavy Knights underneath their breastplates.
You feel a burning heat on your feet as you walk while wearing these.
Many years in the sun has dried out these gloves, you can almost feel them sucking the moisture out of you.
These pants are not very regular. They do however make you feel healthier.
Cold and empty. You aren't sure if anyone flame could reignite this.
A piece of waste taken from the Empyrean Forge. Ordinarily, you'd be quite foolish to want this, but the lingering energies of the forge have enchanted some amount of power into this.
A piece of valuable fuel for many fires. You however? I have no idea what you're going to do with it.
The fire of life burns within you.
It's surprising that this gauntlet has even lasted in the forge for this long.
Even within the creeping recesses of the void, hope can be found.
Explosive power and heat erupt out of this seemingly benign staff.
A useful tool in the forge to stoke the flames. It will probably serve well enough as a weapon.
Far more adept at slipping between armored plates than it is at slicing through your foes.
"Yes. You are fighting 'with fire'. You are technically 'fire fighting', Gary. You are technically not wrong Gary."
A piece of equipment that had fallen off of a forge. It protected workers from the flames before, so it will likely protect you just as well.
A skillful warrior can put such a weapon to good use.
The wood composing this bow has charred over the years of exposure.
This won't kill your foes as much as it will shred them into piece.
The extra-volatile powder this gun uses makes it spurt flames on shot.
A powerful strikes compels the receiver to kneel.
Parry and riposte upon your foes.
This flail seems to have been rather haphazardly forged, but it's quite good at rending through armor because of that.
Dragons may not be real, but that's not enough to stop an enterprising merchant from pumping up his wares to his suckers.
The metal this helmet is forged from is unspectacular, but the inner portions make it surprisingly comfortable in the summer.
The void slowly drips up your legs as you wear this armor.
Heavy armor is difficult to move in, but offers some unique advantages to other equipment.
Scaled armor may not be in fashion any longer, but it's no less effective.

This power source has been depleted for a long time.
This crystal thrums with charge, full of untapped potential.
How is this even possible without destroying the battery? Truly the Ancients mastered many mysteries.
Lighter than air, brighter than starlight, this essence dances in the container.
Triple refined so that only the purest silver was left after the smelting process.
Traditionally used to soothe troubled minds, these buds can unlock alternate methods of viewing the world.
This is a recipe for attuning oneself with the chaotic magic which flows from the Arcana cards.
Attune yourself to the chaotic magic which flows from the Arcana cards by drinking this potion.
Only the finest wines fill Alecksi's cellars.
The power emanating from the crystal feels more agitated, as if it knows something is about to happen.
This crude bone key looks like it would work on one of the Berlaur cages.
An ornate box lined with powerful protections, perfectly sized to fit the Tear of Gaea.
Morgaine's scrawling handwriting shows her descent into semi-coherent madness and her obsession with the Tear of Gaea.
Morgaine's experimental potions for holding back the transformation to becoming a thrall for as long as she could.
These troubling letters plainly state how turning Morgaine into an Upyr would give them access to her magic, and track her current location.
A fine red powder that smells vaguely of onions and clover.
Either through a trick of the light or strange alchemical properties, this liquid changes from red to silver depending on the angle it's held.
It shines from within, bringing hope and burning away all doubts.
These mushrooms look like someone took a handful of crumpled silk and dipped it into blood.
Created by the Builder King, this is the ultimate architectural key.
Swirling in its depths, you catch hints of the dream you had last night, and come to the realization that with this amulet, you could make your dreams become real.
This is a recipe for the first step of curing Upyrism.
While this won't fully cure turning into an Upyr, it is proven to slow down the transformation.
These pungent charms are said to keep all evils at bay.
Fresh and fat and juicy, these rats are clearly well fed.
They look amazingly appetizing, for being made from parts of rats.

string.comment: Quotations represent sarcasm to the player- these items are clearly stolen. The player did the stealing.

resources.string: It isn't theft if no one else wants it, right…?

Radiates a fiery celestial glow channeled through a cosmic alignment to the sun.
Even in strange worlds, every Soulwarden needs their trusty staff.
Reinforced against the raging evil of the Corruption. Imbues confidence in its wearer.
Celestial armor resonating with solar energy.
Reforged in the black fires of Necromancy by a craftsman whose gaze lingers on darker worlds than our own.
Once worn the armor exhibits a peculiar magnetic attraction to its wearer. It's said to have been forged by a grieving parent longing to protect their lost child.
Veins of corruption restrained by ritual and vengeance. Wielded not for glory, but to end what should not live.
What is more intimidating than the sound of silence?
Bound with bone and blackest magick, an unholy ensemble that transforms and transfigures the brave soul entombed within.
Radiates a fiery celestial glow channeled through a cosmic alignment to the sun.
A nightmare born in the death of year's end, crowned and clad in Baalphazu's name.
The treasures of the waves will surely light your way.
A collection of tapestries from distant lands, recovered from shipwrecks.
Their drum beat echoes the sound of marching hooves.

A collection of relics bearing the essence of fallen kings, steeped in sacrifice and forged from marrow, sinew, and regret.
